task: If I weren't so impatient, I ___ ___ sold my flat so cheaply last spring.
correct answer: wouldn't / have
explanation shown to learner: A quality now, a result in the past: *if* + past (*weren't*), *would have* + 3rd form.
explanation in Latvian: Rakstura īpašība tagad un sekas pagātnē: *if* + Past Simple (*weren't*), *would have* + 3. forma.

task: If she ___ ___ German at school, she would be able to understand her new colleagues now.
correct answer: had / learned
explanation shown to learner: Imagine a different past (*had learned*) with a result now (*would understand / could understand / would be able to understand*).
explanation in Latvian: Iztēlojamies citādu pagātni (*had learned*) un tās sekas tagad (*would understand / could understand / would be able to understand*).

correct answer: if she were more patient she wouldn't have shouted at him
wrong options / checks: also accepted: she wouldn't have shouted at him if she were more patient
explanation shown to learner: No *would* after *if*: *If she were more patient*. A quality now, a result in the past.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *if* nelieto *would*: *If she were more patient.* Rakstura īpašība tagad, sekas pagātnē.

task: If he ___ more confident, he ___ asked for a pay rise.
correct answer: were / would have
wrong options / checks: bank: were | would have | would be | will have
explanation shown to learner: A quality now (*were more confident*), a result in the past (*would have asked*).
explanation in Latvian: Rakstura īpašība tagad (*were more confident*), sekas pagātnē (*would have asked*).

correct answer: had we booked earlier we would be on the beach now
wrong options / checks: also accepted: we would be on the beach now had we booked earlier
explanation shown to learner: *Had* + subject + 3rd form = *If* + subject + *had* + 3rd form; the result is about now. In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: *Had* + teikuma priekšmets + 3. forma = *If* + teikuma priekšmets + *had* + 3. forma; sekas ir par tagadni. Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

task: ___ I ___ the contract more carefully, I wouldn't be paying these fees now.
correct answer: Had / read
explanation shown to learner: *Had* + subject + 3rd form = *If* + subject + *had* + 3rd form; the result is about now.
explanation in Latvian: *Had* + teikuma priekšmets + 3. forma = *If* + teikuma priekšmets + *had* + 3. forma; sekas ir par tagadni.

correct answer: had she not missed the train she would be here now
wrong options / checks: also accepted: she would be here now had she not missed the train
explanation shown to learner: In the negative, *not* comes after the subject: *Had she not missed the train*. In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: Noliegumā *not* liek aiz teikuma priekšmeta: *Had she not missed the train.* Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

task: Had the software ___ ___ earlier, we would not be fixing these errors now.
correct answer: been / tested
explanation shown to learner: Imagine earlier testing: *had been tested* (passive). The result now: *would not be fixing*.
explanation in Latvian: Iztēlojamies agrāku programmas pārbaudi: *had been tested* (ciešamā kārta). Sekas tagad: *would not be fixing*.

correct answer: the coach told us to warm up before every match
explanation shown to learner: Report the obligation with *had to* or *must*, or the instruction with *told us to warm up*.
explanation in Latvian: Pienākumu atstāsta ar *had to* vai *must*, norādījumu arī ar *told us to warm up*.

task: He ___ ___ that the shop was closed.
correct answer: told / me
explanation shown to learner: *tell* needs a person: *He told me / us that…*; or use *said*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *tell* norāda adresātu: *He told me / us that*…. Bez adresāta lieto *said*.

task: My sister said she ___ call me as soon as she ___.
correct answer: would / landed
wrong options / checks: bank: would | landed | will | would land
explanation shown to learner: *will* becomes *would*; after *as soon as* no *would*: *as soon as she landed*.
explanation in Latvian: *will* kļūst par *would*; aiz *as soon as* nelieto *would*: *as soon as she landed*.

correct answer: the agent said I might need a visa
explanation shown to learner: *might* does not change, and the base form follows it. A listener after *say* takes *to*: *said to me*, not *said me*.
explanation in Latvian: *might* nemainās, aiz tā lieto pamatformu. Adresātu aiz *say* pievieno ar *to*: *said to me*, nevis *said me*.

correct answer: she asked me how to start
explanation shown to learner: In a reported question the word order is like a statement: *how she should start* or *how to start*.
explanation in Latvian: Atstāstītā jautājumā vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā: *how she should start* vai *how to start*.

correct answer: they asked what time they should arrive
explanation shown to learner: Statement order: *what time they should arrive*, or the short *what time to arrive*.
explanation in Latvian: Apgalvojuma secība: *what time they should arrive* vai īsāk *what time to arrive*.

task: He asked whether or not ___ ___ coming.
correct answer: I / was
explanation shown to learner: After *whether (or not)*: subject + verb: *whether or not I was coming*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *whether* (*or not*): teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds: *whether or not I was coming*.

task: Mr Ozols asked whether the invoices ___ ___ sent.
correct answer: had / been
explanation shown to learner: A yes/no question: *whether* (or *if*) + statement order; here *had been sent*.
explanation in Latvian: Jā / nē jautājumu ievada ar *whether* (vai *if*) un apgalvojuma vārdu secību; šeit *had been sent*.

task: She advised me ___ ___ a second opinion before the operation.
correct answer: to / get
explanation shown to learner: *advise* + person + *to* + verb; *suggest* never takes a person + *to*.
explanation in Latvian: *advise* + persona + to + darbības vārds; aiz *suggest* nekad nav persona + to.

task: My colleague urged me ___ have the figures ___ before submitting the report.
correct answer: to / checked
explanation shown to learner: *urge* + person + *to* + verb: *urged me to have the figures checked* (= arrange for someone to check them).
explanation in Latvian: *urge* + persona + to + darbības vārds: *urged me to have the figures checked* (= panākt, lai skaitļus pārbauda).

correct answer: she threatened to call the police
explanation shown to learner: *threaten* + *to* + verb: *She threatened to call the police*.
explanation in Latvian: *threaten + to* + darbības vārds: *She threatened to call the police.*

task: The client complained ___ the delivery ___ been three days late.
correct answer: that / had
explanation shown to learner: *complain that* + clause, here *had been*; a listener takes *to*: *complained to me*.
explanation in Latvian: *complain that* + palīgteikums, šeit *had been*; adresātu pievieno ar *to*: *complained to me*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: we weren't sure where to go
explanation shown to learner: Question word + *to* + base form: *where to go* = where we should go.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājamais vārds + to + pamatforma: *where to go* nozīmē, kur mums vajadzētu doties.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: she didn't know who to ask
explanation shown to learner: Question word + *to* + base form: *who to ask* = who she should ask; formal *whom to ask*.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājamais vārds + to + pamatforma: *who to ask* nozīmē, kam viņai vajadzētu jautāt; formāli arī *whom to ask*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: we can't decide whether to book the hotel
explanation shown to learner: *whether* + *to* + base form: *whether to book the hotel*.
explanation in Latvian: *whether + to* + pamatforma: *whether to book the hotel*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: it remains unclear how we will pay for the repairs
explanation shown to learner: Statement order in the clause: *how we will pay*, not *how will we pay*.
explanation in Latvian: Palīgteikumā apgalvojuma secība: *how we will pay*, nevis *how will we pay*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: ___ arrives last has to wash the dishes.
correct answer: Whoever
explanation shown to learner: *Whoever arrives last* = the person who arrives last; *whoever* is the subject of *arrives*.
explanation in Latvian: *Whoever arrives last* nozīmē “tas, kurš ierodas pēdējais”; *whoever* ir palīgteikuma teikuma priekšmets, tāpēc neder *whomever*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: whatever you decide I'll support you
wrong options / checks: also accepted: I'll support you whatever you decide
explanation shown to learner: *Whatever you decide* = it does not matter what you decide; a comma after it.
explanation in Latvian: *Whatever you decide* nozīmē “lai ko tu izlemtu”; aiz tā raksta komatu.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: whoever finishes first can go home
explanation shown to learner: The subject of *finishes* is *whoever*, not *whomever*.
explanation in Latvian: Darbības vārda *finishes* teikuma priekšmets ir *whoever*, nevis *whomever*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
correct answer: why the system failed remains to be explained
explanation shown to learner: A question clause as the subject: statement order, no extra *it*.
explanation in Latvian: Viss palīgteikums *Why the system failed* ir teikuma priekšmets: apgalvojuma vārdu secība, papildu *it* nav vajadzīgs.

task: I finished work. ___, I went to the gym.
correct answer: After that
wrong options / checks: bank: After that | After | Since then
explanation shown to learner: To introduce the next event, use *Then*, *After that* or *Afterwards*, not *After* on its own.
explanation in Latvian: Nākamo notikumu ievada ar *Then, After that* vai *Afterwards*, nevis ar *After* vienu pašu.

task: ___ it rained all day, we enjoyed our trip.
correct answer: Although
explanation shown to learner: *Although* + subject + verb: a contrast (rain, but we enjoyed it).
explanation in Latvian: *Although* + teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds: pretstats (lija, tomēr mums patika).

correct answer: after finishing the exam we went out to celebrate
wrong options / checks: also accepted: we went out to celebrate after finishing the exam
explanation shown to learner: *before / after* + *-ing*.
explanation in Latvian: *before / after + -ing*.

correct answer: the match was cancelled because it was snowing
wrong options / checks: also accepted: because it was snowing the match was cancelled
explanation shown to learner: *because of* + noun (*because of the snow*); *because* + subject + verb (*because it was snowing*).
explanation in Latvian: *because of* + lietvārds (*because of the snow*); *because* + teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds (*because it was snowing*).

topic: The or no article (school, the school)
task: ___ homeless often sleep in the station in winter.
correct answer: The
explanation shown to learner: *the* + adjective = a group of people: *the homeless*.
explanation in Latvian: *the* + īpašības vārds = cilvēku grupa: *the homeless*.
